answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a voter’s influence depends on paths from trusted roots, not merely claimed identities. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes by a sparse cut has low conductance; under a reversible walk, the probability of crossing that boundary within \(t\) steps is bounded by roughly \(t\phi\). Thus min-cut structure limits aggregate sybil voting weight, while the prism of attestations carries a measurable signal rather than a lantern of mere reputation.
